scope: Prerequisite for the actual chat widget, not a replacement for it: authenticated channel-message, member and override caches must never project an old account's text or permissions into a new native surface.

Credential-free synchronous owner and login-generation events break auth/crypto/store import cycles and invalidate account-owned caches even for same-user reauthentication. Normal access-token renewal is not a login-generation boundary.

Member and channel-override sources expose explicit current-owner/current-generation successful-load status. Failed refreshes may retain rows for existing UI continuity but cannot authorize sensitive projections.

useChannelPermissions exposes a separate fail-closed authorizationResolved flag requiring successful matching member and override snapshots and the current member. Existing optimistic composer permsResolved behavior is preserved; neither flag grants permissions by itself.

The transport captures owner/generation before token/ticket awaits, rejects old socket callbacks and coalesces owner/generation boundaries into one fresh connection. This closes the case where an old socket event starts after the new session already exists.

Dispatch also rechecks the originating connection predicate between awaited domain handlers. Channel decrypt passes its captured guard into Signal/PreKey and SenderKey operations; session/sender/trust/plaintext-cache writes abort on auth boundaries, and stale spam registration completions cannot affect the current session.
The actual chat widget, composer IPC, spam/ignored-content parity and video/stream widgets remain incomplete. No dormant chat toggle or fake functioning chat widget was introduced.

open: Release blocker: persistent crypto records still share the global mqvi_e2ee IndexedDB namespace. e2eeStore has an existing registration-user mismatch guard that clears the shared database, but no durable per-account partition/archive. Matching claimed registration checks device ID, not public identity-key equality; missing/ambiguous provenance and existing destructive account-switch behavior require preservation-first migration/recovery work. In-flight write fences alone do not solve stored-record ownership. No database deletion or migration was performed by this slice.
